blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-migration-1 (Irreversible DROP COLUMN with no down migration or backup) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-migration-2 (Public JSON field renamed with no BREAKING mark) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
-- Drop the column left from the 2023 import.
ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN legacy_email;
findings.recommendation: Add `migrations/0005_drop_legacy_email.down.sql` (re-adding `legacy_email TEXT`, as 0004 has its own `.down.sql`) and, since the down cannot restore the values, copy the column's data to a backup table or export before dropping it — or state in the plan why the data is disposable and how to recover. "Not written since 2023" does not mean empty: existing rows still hold the imported emails.
findings.title: Irreversible DROP COLUMN with no down migration or backup

findings.recommendation: `Account` is a public HTTP API type: its `user_name` field becomes `userName`, so every API consumer reading `user_name` breaks silently. Mark the item **BREAKING** in the proposal's release note, with what consumers must do (read `userName` instead), and treat it as a major version change.
findings.title: Public JSON field renamed with no BREAKING mark

findings.recommendation: Write it as a **BREAKING** item naming the field (`user_name` → `userName`) and the consumer action; also add an item for the dropped `users.legacy_email` column, which the release note does not mention.
findings.title: Release note announces the rename as a plain change

findings.recommendation: Consumers get no time to move: the old key disappears in the same release that introduces the new one. Expand then contract — serialize both `user_name` and `userName` for a deprecation period (e.g. a second field or a custom `Serialize`), announce the removal of `user_name`, then drop it in a later release. Add a test asserting the serialized keys.
findings.title: Rename shipped without a deprecation or side-by-side period

findings.evidence:
- [x] 1.1 Migration 0005, verified by `sqlx migrate run` on a copy of production
- [x] 1.2 camelCase account field, verified by `cargo test api`
findings.recommendation: The diff adds no test: nothing checks that 0005 can be rolled back, nor the serialized key names of `Account`. Add a serialization test for `Account` and exercise the down migration once it exists.
findings.title: No test covers the migration path
